sinks.rationale: child_process.exec(command) runs the command string through /bin/sh (cmd.exe on Windows); any attacker text in it is shell syntax.
Synchronous form of child_process.exec; the command string reaches the same shell interpretation path.

child_process.spawn(command, args) executes the named program directly; an attacker-chosen command is arbitrary program execution even without shell:true, and with shell:true the string is shell syntax.
Synchronous form of child_process.spawn; same command-selection exposure.
child_process.execFile(file, args) executes the named file without a shell by default; an attacker-chosen file path is still arbitrary program execution.
Synchronous form of child_process.execFile; same program-selection exposure.
child_process.fork(modulePath) spawns a new Node process running the named module; an attacker-chosen path executes arbitrary reachable JavaScript.
Global eval(x) evaluates its argument as JavaScript in the caller's scope; attacker text is attacker code.

new Function(...args, body) compiles every argument into a function (leading arguments are parameter names, the last is the body); a tainted value in any declared position is compiled as code. Real call sites rarely exceed four arguments.
vm.runInThisContext(code) compiles and runs the code string in the current global context; the vm module is not a security boundary.
vm.runInNewContext(code) compiles and runs the code string in a fresh context that can still reach the host process; attacker code executes.
vm.runInContext(code, context) compiles and runs the code string inside the given contextified object; same execution exposure as the other vm.run* forms.
new vm.Script(code) compiles the code string; every runIn* method of the resulting script executes it.
vm.compileFunction(code, params) compiles the code string into a callable function body.
fs.readFile(path, ...) opens whatever path it is given; attacker path segments read files outside the intended directory.
Synchronous form of fs.readFile; same path exposure.
fs.writeFile(file, data, ...) creates or truncates whatever path it is given; attacker path segments write outside the intended directory.
Synchronous form of fs.writeFile; same path exposure.
fs.createReadStream(path) opens the named path for streaming reads — the common Express file-serving shape.
fs.createWriteStream(path) opens the named path for streaming writes; attacker path segments plant files outside the intended directory.

sanitizers.rationale: path.basename strips directory components, the common containment idiom — but its return can still be '..' (path.basename('/a/..') === '..') and on POSIX it leaves backslash sequences intact, so it tags the hop rather than killing the class.

propagators.rationale: path.join(...paths) concatenates every argument into the returned path; taint in any segment survives.
path.resolve(...paths) folds every argument into the returned absolute path; an attacker segment can still escape via absolute-path override or dot-dot.
path.normalize(path) rewrites separators and dot segments but returns the same attacker-chosen location.
Global decodeURIComponent returns a decoded copy of its argument — decoding often RE-ARMS encoded attack bytes.
Global decodeURI returns a decoded copy of its argument, same re-arming behaviour as decodeURIComponent.
querystring.unescape(str) percent-decodes its argument (legacy but still shipped); decoded attacker bytes flow onward.
Buffer.from(input) wraps its argument's bytes in a Buffer; the content is unchanged attacker data.
JSON.parse(text) returns structured data whose string leaves are substrings of the attacker input.
